---
params:
  x:
title: "\\fontsize{14}{16}\\selectfont Zuwachs auf Betriebsebene -- Wiederholungsinventur"
classoption:
  - a4paper
geometry:
  - portrait
  - "left=1.5cm,right=1.5cm,top=1.5cm,bottom=2cm"
fontsize: 10pt
header-includes:
  - \usepackage{siunitx}
  - \sisetup{output-decimal-marker = {,}, group-separator = {\,}}
  - \usepackage{booktabs}
  - \usepackage{longtable}
  - \usepackage{makecell}
  - \usepackage{array}
  # Custom column type with extra right-side gap, used between
  # column 3 (einzelbaumbasiert / zv (m^3/ha/J)) and column 4
  # (ertragsgeschichtlich / zv (m^3/J)) so the two blocks visually
  # separate. The @{...} declaration replaces the default \tabcolsep
  # separator with the explicit \hspace, so we set it a bit wider than
  # the default 6pt to add ~6pt of visible gap.
  - \newcolumntype{G}{r@{\hspace{2em}}}
  # Suppress page numbers. The output is always a single page by
  # design (one summary table + meta block + footnote). \maketitle
  # otherwise applies \thispagestyle{plain} which prints a centred
  # "1" at the bottom -- we override both `plain` and the global
  # pagestyle to render an empty footer instead. If a future variant
  # ever spans multiple pages, swap this for a conditional setup
  # based on `lastpage` + `fancyhdr`.
  - \usepackage{fancyhdr}
  - \pagestyle{empty}
  - \fancypagestyle{plain}{\fancyhf{}\renewcommand{\headrulewidth}{0pt}}
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
oo <- options(knitr.kable.NA = "", fe_spec_lang = "ger")
```

```{r helpers}
# --- LaTeX cell formatters --------------------------------------------
# Decimal-point alignment via manual `\hphantom{}` padding inside plain
# `r`-aligned columns. siunitx S columns with `table-format` and
# `separate-uncertainty` proved unreliable inside kableExtra's
# pack_rows output, so we do the padding ourselves: deterministic, no
# external dependencies on column-type parsing.
#
# Per column, we know the maximum integer-part width across all rows
# (computed once outside, see build-unified-table chunk). For each cell:
#   - prepend `\hphantom{00}` for each missing integer-part digit so
#     the value's decimal lands at a fixed column position;
#   - if a CI is present, do the same for its integer part;
#   - if no CI, append a right-side `\hphantom{...}` matching the
#     width of " ± XXX,Y" so cells without CI still have the same
#     total width as cells with CI -- this keeps the column visually
#     coherent.

# Integer-part digit count (e.g. 5.9 -> 1, 190.1 -> 3, 0.0 -> 1).
n_int_digits <- function(v) {
  if (length(v) == 0L || all(is.na(v))) return(1L)
  v <- v[!is.na(v)]
  vals <- floor(abs(v))
  strs <- formatC(vals, format = "d", big.mark = "")
  max(nchar(strs), 1L)
}

# All \hphantom{} contents are wrapped in \textnormal{} so the phantom
# width is measured in the upright/regular font, even when the cell is
# later wrapped in \textbf{} (which kableExtra::row_spec does for the
# "Summe" rows). Without \textnormal{}, bold digit metrics make the
# Summe cells minimally wider than the rest, and r-alignment pulls the
# Summe value visibly to the left.

# A "\num{X.Y}" call with leading `\hphantom{0..0}` so the decimal
# marker ends up at a fixed offset from the left of the cell.
pad_num <- function(val, max_int, digits) {
  v_int  <- floor(abs(val))
  v_n    <- nchar(formatC(v_int, format = "d", big.mark = ""))
  pad    <- max_int - v_n
  prefix <- if (pad > 0L) {
    paste0("\\hphantom{\\textnormal{", strrep("0", pad), "}}")
  } else ""
  paste0(prefix, sprintf("\\num{%.*f}", digits, val))
}

# Build one fully-padded LaTeX cell. NA-val -> empty cell (rendered as
# a phantom that matches the full width of a value-only cell, so the
# column geometry stays consistent across rows).
fmt_cell <- function(val, ci, max_val_int, max_ci_int, digits) {
  if (is.na(val)) {
    # Fully empty cell: phantom of "VVV,Y \pm CCC,Y" width
    return(paste0(
      "\\hphantom{\\textnormal{",
      strrep("0", max_val_int), ",", strrep("0", digits),
      "\\,\\ensuremath{\\pm}\\,",
      strrep("0", max_ci_int), ",", strrep("0", digits),
      "}}"
    ))
  }
  val_part <- pad_num(val, max_val_int, digits)
  if (is.na(ci)) {
    # Value-only: right-pad with phantom of "\,\pm\,CCC,Y" width
    rp <- paste0(
      "\\hphantom{\\textnormal{\\,\\ensuremath{\\pm}\\,",
      strrep("0", max_ci_int), ",", strrep("0", digits), "}}"
    )
    return(paste0(val_part, rp))
  }
  ci_part <- pad_num(ci, max_ci_int, digits)
  paste0(val_part, "\\,\\ensuremath{\\pm}\\,", ci_part)
}

# Vectorise: build a character vector of LaTeX cells, one per row.
vfmt_cell <- function(val, ci, max_val_int, max_ci_int, digits) {
  mapply(
    fmt_cell, val, ci,
    MoreArgs = list(max_val_int = max_val_int,
                    max_ci_int  = max_ci_int,
                    digits      = digits)
  )
}

# Escape the LaTeX-special characters that realistically appear in
# user-supplied strings (subtitle, fill_option name, species label).
# The big one is '_' which is a math subscript and triggers
# "Missing $ inserted" in text mode.
latex_escape <- function(x) {
  if (length(x) == 0L) return(x)
  x <- as.character(x)
  x <- gsub("([&%$#_])", "\\\\\\1", x)
  x
}

# species_group as a printable label (uses fe_spec_lang option). The
# total row is marked separately and gets the "Summe" label.
fmt_species <- function(sg, is_total) {
  out <- latex_escape(format(sg))
  out[is_total] <- "Summe"
  out
}
```

```{r meta-block, results = "asis"}
m <- params$x$meta

# Forstbetrieb name (= optional user_subtitle), centred just below
# the title. \maketitle has a large bottom skip plus \begin{center}
# adds a paragraph break; \vspace{-3em} closes both gaps so the
# Forstbetrieb name sits right under the title. All user-supplied
# strings may contain underscores -- escape before emitting.
if (!is.null(m$user_subtitle)) {
  cat("\\vspace{-3em}\\begin{center}\n",
      "{\\large\\textbf{", latex_escape(m$user_subtitle), "}}\n",
      "\\end{center}\n", sep = "")
}

# Meta block, flushleft. The two survey years are right-aligned with
# each other inside a small two-column tabular ("Inventur:" label and
# "Vorhergehende Inventur:" label both flush left; both years end at
# the same horizontal position). Period, method, and fill_option
# follow as plain flushleft lines below.
method_str <- if (!is.null(m$method)) {
  latex_escape(m$method)
} else {
  "nicht angegeben"
}
fill_option_str <- latex_escape(m$fill_option)

# Gesamtfläche and Inventurpunkte of the *current* inventory (A + B).
# These go into a third tabular column that is filled only on the
# current-inventory row -- the year column (col 2) therefore stays as
# narrow as before, so the two right-aligned years do not shift.
area_curr_str <- format(round(m$plot_match_stats$area_total_2nd_ha),
                        big.mark = ".", decimal.mark = ",",
                        scientific = FALSE)
n_curr        <- m$plot_match_stats$n_total_2nd

cat("\\begin{flushleft}\n")
cat(sprintf(
  paste0(
    # `@{}` at the very left of the tabular column spec removes the
    # default \tabcolsep on the left so the tabular starts flush with
    # the rest of the meta block; without it the "Inventur:" and
    # "Vorhergehende Inventur:" labels sit indented relative to the
    # plain flushleft lines below. The trailing `@{}l` adds a third,
    # left-aligned column carrying the current inventory's area and
    # point count; `@{}` keeps col 2 (year) flush against it and the
    # cell leads with an explicit \hspace so the gap is controlled.
    "\\begin{tabular}{@{}l@{ }r@{}l}\n",
    "\\textbf{Inventur:} & %d & \\hspace{2em}\\textbf{Gesamtfläche:} %s ha",
    "\\hspace{1.5em}\\textbf{Inventurpunkte:} %d \\\\\n",
    "\\textbf{Vorhergehende Inventur:} & %d & \\\\\n",
    "\\end{tabular}\\\\\n",
    "\\textbf{Periode:} %d Jahre\\\\\n",
    "\\textbf{Berechnungsmethode:} %s\\\\\n",
    "\\textbf{Ergänzungsmethode:} %s\n"
  ),
  m$inv_year_curr,
  area_curr_str,
  n_curr,
  m$inv_year_prev,
  m$period_yr,
  method_str,
  fill_option_str
))
cat("\\end{flushleft}\n")
```

```{r build-unified-table, results = "asis"}
# --- Pre-compute per-column max integer widths ------------------------
# The pad widths are shared across all three sections so the value
# commas align column-wide, not just within a section.
tm <- params$x$table_matched
ts <- params$x$table_2nd_only
tc <- params$x$table_combined

max_int_val_yr <- max(
  n_int_digits(c(tm$iv_m3_yr_total_st,  tm$iv_m3_yr_total_sum,
                 ts$iv_m3_yr_total_st,
                 tc$iv_m3_yr_total_st,  tc$iv_m3_yr_total_sum))
)
max_int_ci_yr  <- max(
  n_int_digits(c(tm$ci95_iv_m3_yr_total_st, tm$ci95_iv_m3_yr_total_sum))
)
max_int_val_ha <- max(
  n_int_digits(c(tm$iv_m3_ha_yr_st,  tm$iv_m3_ha_yr_sum,
                 ts$iv_m3_ha_yr_st,
                 tc$iv_m3_ha_yr_st,  tc$iv_m3_ha_yr_sum))
)
max_int_ci_ha  <- max(
  n_int_digits(c(tm$ci95_iv_m3_ha_yr_st, tm$ci95_iv_m3_ha_yr_sum))
)

# Build the five-column data frame for one input table. sum_block = FALSE
# (table_2nd_only) leaves the summaric columns empty -- rendered as
# full-width phantoms so the column geometry stays intact.
build_rows <- function(tbl, sum_block = TRUE) {
  spec <- fmt_species(tbl$species_group, tbl$is_total_row)

  st_yr_tot <- vfmt_cell(tbl$iv_m3_yr_total_st, tbl$ci95_iv_m3_yr_total_st,
                         max_int_val_yr, max_int_ci_yr, 1)
  st_yr_ha  <- vfmt_cell(tbl$iv_m3_ha_yr_st,    tbl$ci95_iv_m3_ha_yr_st,
                         max_int_val_ha, max_int_ci_ha, 2)
  if (sum_block) {
    sum_yr_tot <- vfmt_cell(tbl$iv_m3_yr_total_sum, tbl$ci95_iv_m3_yr_total_sum,
                             max_int_val_yr, max_int_ci_yr, 1)
    sum_yr_ha  <- vfmt_cell(tbl$iv_m3_ha_yr_sum,    tbl$ci95_iv_m3_ha_yr_sum,
                             max_int_val_ha, max_int_ci_ha, 2)
  } else {
    # 2nd_only: summaric block is empty by contract. Render as
    # full-width phantom so the column width matches the other sections.
    na_vec <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(tbl))
    sum_yr_tot <- vfmt_cell(na_vec, na_vec, max_int_val_yr, max_int_ci_yr, 1)
    sum_yr_ha  <- vfmt_cell(na_vec, na_vec, max_int_val_ha, max_int_ci_ha, 2)
  }

  data.frame(
    Artgruppe = spec,
    v1 = st_yr_tot, v2 = st_yr_ha,
    v3 = sum_yr_tot, v4 = sum_yr_ha,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

df_m <- build_rows(tm, sum_block = TRUE)
df_s <- build_rows(ts, sum_block = FALSE)
df_c <- build_rows(tc, sum_block = TRUE)

df <- rbind(df_m, df_s, df_c)
n_m <- nrow(df_m); n_s <- nrow(df_s); n_c <- nrow(df_c)

hdr_iv_yr <- "zv (m\\textsuperscript{3}/J)"
hdr_iv_ha <- "zv (m\\textsuperscript{3}/ha/J)"

# Plain right-aligned columns. The cells already carry `\hphantom{}`
# padding so all rows have identical width and the value commas line
# up at the same horizontal offset.
k <- knitr::kable(
  df,
  format    = "latex",
  booktabs  = TRUE,
  escape    = FALSE,
  # Col 3 uses the custom G type (= r + extra right-side gap) so the
  # ertragsgeschichtlich block (cols 4-5) sits visibly separated from
  # the einzelbaumbasiert block (cols 2-3). The G column type is
  # defined in the YAML header-includes.
  align     = c("l", "r", "G", "r", "r"),
  col.names = c("Artgruppe", hdr_iv_yr, hdr_iv_ha, hdr_iv_yr, hdr_iv_ha),
  linesep   = ""
)

# Section labels with per-section Inventurpunkt count and area.
# kableExtra::pack_rows() applies an extra sub("\\\\", ...) pass even
# when escape = FALSE that strips backslashes from all but the first
# LaTeX command in the label -- so we avoid LaTeX commands in the
# label entirely and format the German decimal comma in R. The
# downside: the parenthesised tail inherits the bold wrap.
ps <- m$plot_match_stats
fmt_ha <- function(x) gsub("\\.", ",", sprintf("%.1f", x))
hdr_A <- sprintf(
  "Wiederholt gemessene Inventurpunkte (A) (n = %d; %s ha)",
  ps$n_matched, fmt_ha(ps$area_matched_ha)
)
hdr_B <- sprintf(
  "Nur in der aktuellen Inventur erfasste Punkte (B) -- BWI 3-Rückwärtsschätzung (n = %d; %s ha)",
  ps$n_2nd_only, fmt_ha(ps$area_2nd_only_ha)
)
hdr_C <- sprintf(
  "Gesamtbetrieb = A + B (n = %d; %s ha)",
  ps$n_total_2nd, fmt_ha(ps$area_total_2nd_ha)
)

# Block headers (single-tree / summaric) -- once, at the top of the
# unified table. The section A label is then stacked *above* this row
# via a second add_header_above call so it sits immediately under the
# \toprule (not under the column-header midrule). Sections B and C
# keep their pack_rows labels in the normal mid-table position.
k <- k |> kableExtra::add_header_above(
  c(" " = 1,
    "einzelbaumbasiert"    = 2,
    "ertragsgeschichtlich" = 2),
  escape = FALSE
)

hdr_A_above <- stats::setNames(5L, hdr_A)
k <- k |> kableExtra::add_header_above(
  hdr_A_above,
  escape = FALSE,
  bold   = TRUE,
  align  = "l",
  line   = FALSE
)

# Bold the "Summe" rows at the end of each section and put a
# midrule below Summe(A) and Summe(B) so the next section header
# (B and C respectively) is visually separated. We deliberately
# do NOT add an explicit \addlinespace here: kableExtra::pack_rows()
# already prefixes its label row with \addlinespace[0.3em], so the
# pack_rows label for sections B and C sits ~0.3em below the
# preceding \midrule. The section A label gets a matching ~0.4em
# strut appended above (see add_header_above), keeping the gap
# below the rule-above-label visually consistent across sections.
xs_section_break <- "\\midrule"

k <- k |>
  kableExtra::row_spec(
    n_m, bold = TRUE,
    extra_latex_after = xs_section_break
  ) |>
  kableExtra::row_spec(
    n_m + n_s, bold = TRUE,
    extra_latex_after = xs_section_break
  ) |>
  kableExtra::row_spec(
    n_m + n_s + n_c, bold = TRUE
  ) |>
  kableExtra::row_spec(
    c(n_m - 1L, n_m + n_s - 1L, n_m + n_s + n_c - 1L),
    extra_latex_after = "\\midrule"
  )

# Below each section header we add a bit of breathing room before the
# first data row via extra_latex_after = "\\addlinespace[0.4em]".
# Section C additionally gets a sub-header row spanning cols 4-5 that
# announces the mixed methodology of the rightmost block in the
# Gesamtbetrieb: A's ertragsgeschichtliche Bilanz + B's BWI 3-Schätzung.
# All three sections use the default latex_gap_space, so the vertical
# spacing between sections is uniform (the previous "1em" before C
# made the gap under Summe(B) visibly larger than under Summe(A)).
xla_AB <- "\\addlinespace[0.4em]"
# Wrap the section C sub-header text over two lines via \makecell.
# Single line was wider than the natural cols 4+5 width and forced
# both columns to expand: that pushed the cols-4-5 visual gap noticeably
# wider than the cols-2-3 gap (right-aligned content sits at the right
# edge of each column, so a wider column means more leading whitespace
# on the left, which reads as extra space between adjacent columns).
xla_C  <- paste0(
  " & & & \\multicolumn{2}{c}{\\makecell{ertragsgeschichtlich \\\\",
  " und BWI 3-Schätzung}}",
  " \\\\\n\\cmidrule(lr){4-5}\n\\addlinespace[0.4em]"
)

k <- k |>
  kableExtra::pack_rows(
    hdr_B,
    n_m + 1, n_m + n_s,
    escape = FALSE, bold = TRUE, latex_align = "l",
    extra_latex_after = xla_AB
  ) |>
  kableExtra::pack_rows(
    hdr_C,
    n_m + n_s + 1, n_m + n_s + n_c,
    escape = FALSE, bold = TRUE, latex_align = "l",
    extra_latex_after = xla_C
  ) |>
  # pack_rows indents its grouped rows with \hspace{1em} automatically.
  # Section A is added via add_header_above (not pack_rows), so its data
  # rows would sit flush left while the section B and A+B data rows
  # carry the indent. Apply the same indent to section A explicitly so
  # all three sections look consistent.
  kableExtra::add_indent(seq_len(n_m))

k_styled <- k |> kableExtra::kable_styling(
  font_size     = 9,
  latex_options = c("hold_position"),
  position      = "center"
)

# Two post-processing steps on the final LaTeX, both needed because
# kableExtra's add_header_above() and pack_rows() run their label
# strings through a str_replace-based escape pipeline that strips
# backslashes from any embedded LaTeX command -- so we can't put the
# struts/line-breaks into the label itself.
#
# (1) Add a small \addlinespace below the section A label row so the
#     block-header row gets some breathing room from it.
#
# (2) Wrap the section B label in \makecell with a line break. Its
#     full text "Nur in der aktuellen Inventur erfasste Punkte (B) --
#     BWI 3-Rückwärtsschätzung (n = X; Y,Z ha)" is so wide as a single
#     \multicolumn{5}{l}{...} row that LaTeX expands the tabular
#     columns to fit it, which in turn pulls cols 4 and 5 visibly
#     apart. Splitting after "Rückwärtsschätzung" keeps the same
#     information without forcing the table wider than the natural
#     column widths.
k_styled <- as.character(k_styled)
k_styled <- sub(
  "(Wiederholt gemessene Inventurpunkte[^\n]*\n)",
  "\\1\\\\addlinespace[0.4em]\n",
  k_styled
)
k_styled <- sub(
  paste0(
    "\\{\\\\textbf\\{(Nur in der aktuellen Inventur erfasste Punkte ",
    "\\(B\\) -- BWI 3-Rückwärtsschätzung)",
    " (\\(n = [0-9]+; [^)]+\\))\\}\\}"
  ),
  "{\\\\textbf{\\\\makecell[l]{\\1 \\\\\\\\ \\2}}}",
  k_styled
)
cat(k_styled)
```

```{r ci-footnote, results = "asis"}
# Footnote: clarify that the ± values are 95% CI, and that they are
# only well-defined for the matched (A) section. Wrap in a flushleft
# environment so pandoc treats the block as raw LaTeX -- otherwise
# the {\small\itshape ...} group delimiters are emitted as literal
# braces in the PDF.
cat("\\begin{flushleft}\n")
cat("\\vspace{0.5em}\n")
cat("\\small\\itshape Alle Volumenangaben verstehen sich als ",
    "Erntefestmeter ohne Rinde (Efm o.R.).\n",
    sep = "")
cat("\\par\\vspace{0.3em}\n")
cat("Die mit \\ensuremath{\\pm} angegebenen Werte ",
    "sind 95\\,\\%-Konfidenzintervalle der Zuwachswerte; sie sind nur ",
    "bei den wiederholt gemessenen Inventurpunkten (Tabelle A) ",
    "sinnvoll bestimmbar.\n",
    sep = "")
cat("\\par\\vspace{0.3em}\n")
cat("Bei kleinen Stichprobenumfängen können beim ",
    "ertragsgeschichtlichen Zuwachs und bei der Berechnungsmethode ",
    "\"rep\\_classic\" negative Zuwachswerte auftreten. ",
    "Das ist statistisch korrekt.\n",
    sep = "")
cat("\\end{flushleft}\n")
```
